name: Andorhal approach road (the flat, the walled lane, the rise)
region: Lordaeron, the south road from below Strahnbrad down to the crest above Andorhal

sensoryProfile.sight: Below Strahnbrad the road runs nearly empty (an army wagon going up, a boy with a switch driving geese); on the flat farm lanes feed it and it fills with carts heaped with roped sacks going in and empties rattling out; hen crates shedding white feathers. Past the next farm it runs between orchard walls (old stone, moss along the coping), then the backs of barns and long low sheds built to the road's edge; carts take turns at the narrow places. The walls end at the top of a long low rise.
sensoryProfile.sound: Cart wheels, drivers cursing at a wheel in a rut; two women talking in the middle of the road; pack mules.
sensoryProfile.smell: Dust from loaded carts that has nowhere to go between walls, fine and pale, hanging at face height, tasting sour like flour left in a damp sack; no wind.
sensoryProfile.touch: The drag comes up all at once in the walled stretch: pressure in the head like diving deep, ears hurting, teeth chattering in the heat, frost on bare fingertips.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: Ordinary traffic into a city while the sickness thickens underneath. Every farm lane adds another thread of lateness to the drag.

establishedFacts.fact: The road is the 'back way' into Andorhal. At the bottom of the hill, per the tally-man, the carts bear off left for the yards; the party keeps straight on to the market gate. A militia post stands just inside the gate on the left with a bench outside the door. The gate on this road is the smaller one. A broad straight road to the right, with a longer line of wagons, runs to a bigger gate: the King's road.

The Thalassian horses shy and do not settle in the walled lane: Sylvanas's scrapes her boot on the wall; Cyndia's half turns, ears flat; Jaina's mare backs, sidesteps toward the ditch. At the ring stones in Ch1-2 they sidestepped once and stood; here they keep shying and go on crabwise with the whites of their eyes showing. Both rangers calm them in low voices.
Jaina's nosebleed and frost happen in the walled stretch before the rise. The party rides through it without stopping.

eventsHere.event: The tally-man is stopped, names Captain Havel and the militia post by the market gate, and says the farewell 'May the stars keep your road'; Sylvanas turns in the saddle; Jaina reads 'nothing but a tired clerk'.
The drag and the horses break; Jaina refuses to dismount and rides on to the rise.
